fields.description: The dyed fabric this row is. A Link, unlike Moodboard Surplus Fabric's fab_code, because a dyed recommendation IS one catalogue row: moodboard_dyed_recommender returns its docname as `id`, and that docname is the row's identity here. Two sent items carrying the same id are the same row and collapse. `code` cannot serve instead — 14,334 distinct codes across 24,838 rows, so it is not unique.
fields.label: Dyed Fabric

fields.description: Whether this fabric is on the board. All recommendations are stored; the user's picks are marked selected. Mirrors Moodboard Surplus Fabric — a fabric the user passed over stays as an unselected row, so re-running the recommender is not what removes it.
fields.label: Selected

fields.description: How the fabric got onto the board: 'recommended' (moodboard_dyed_recommender.recommend) or 'library' (browsed from catalogue()). Library picks carry no match_score / reason / brief attribution, so the UI needs to tell them apart rather than render them as 0-scored recommendations.
fields.label: Source

fields.description: Position in the recommender's returned order (0-based), preserved so the board can re-render the ranking it was shown.
fields.label: Rank

fields.description: Client-side row id, echoed back untouched. Legacy of the get_matching_fabrics flow; the recommender does not send one.
fields.label: Source Id

fields.description: 0-100. The LLM re-rank's score where it picked the fabric, else the deterministic ranking's. Distinct from fit_score, which is the scorer's own number and survives the re-rank untouched.
fields.label: Match Score

fields.description: 'llm' when the LLM re-rank picked it, 'score' when it was backfilled from the deterministic ranking.
fields.label: Match Source

fields.description: The LLM's written rationale. Promoted to a column (rather than left in `recommendation`) because it is what a user asks about later.
fields.label: Reason

fields.description: JSON array of strings, e.g. ["undyed"].
fields.label: Caveats

fields.description: The deterministic scorer's 0-100 fit, before any LLM re-rank. Kept beside match_score because the two answer different questions: how well the cloth fits the spec, versus where the recommender chose to rank it.
fields.label: Fit Score

fields.description: The fit_score's components (construction / composition / gsm / stretch_penalty / color_penalty), as returned. JSON, never queried — it is shown when a user asks why a fabric scored what it did.
fields.label: Score Breakdown

fields.description: The fabric code. NOT unique across the catalogue — see `fabric` for why identity lives there.
fields.label: Code

fields.description: The batch the swatch is keyed on. Image URLs are not stored — they are rebuilt from this on read as plain public asset URLs (never presigned, so the client can cache them), which is also why a re-photographed batch appears without rewriting anything here.
fields.label: Batch

fields.description: The raw construction string the fabric was scored on — clean_quality falling back to quality, whichever the recommender read.
fields.label: Quality

fields.description: The classified construction family (jersey, rib, interlock, ...), as the shared surplus_recommender vocabulary read it.
fields.label: Construction Family

fields.description: JSON array of strings.
fields.label: Texture Tags

fields.description: Gauge ratio for a structured construction, e.g. '2x1' for a rib. Null where the construction has none.
fields.label: Structure Ratio

fields.description: Legacy column from the get_matching_fabrics flow. The recommender sends the blend as `composition`; this is written from it too, so a client that mapped `blend` keeps working.
fields.label: Blend

fields.description: The raw blend string as catalogued, e.g. '95% Cotton 5% Spandex'.
fields.label: Composition

fields.description: Fibre shares as a JSON object, e.g. {"cotton": 95.0, "elastane": 5.0}. Rescaled to total 100 by the recommender, so it will not always echo the raw string's numbers.
fields.label: Composition %

fields.description: This fabric's colour. A scalar, not surplus's colourway list: one dyed catalogue row is one colour. Empty on every row in the catalogue today, which is why needs_dyeing comes back true across the board.
fields.label: Colour

fields.description: The brief palette colour this fabric already answers, when it was colour-matched. Null for a fabric chosen on construction alone — which is every fabric today, the catalogue's `color` column being empty.
fields.label: Matched Palette Colour Id

fields.description: No colour recorded, or an RFD shade, so the cloth could be taken to any palette colour. True on every row today.
fields.label: Needs Dyeing

fields.description: All-in per-kg cost of the Fabric Master this fabric was matched to, loss % included. A specification's cost to MAKE — there is deliberately no price beside it, because a catalogue entry is not cloth that was bought for a number.
fields.label: Price From Fabric Masters

fields.description: The matched Fabric Master's docname. Data, not a Link: this is a snapshot of what the recommender returned, and a Fabric Master deleted later must not make the whole board unsaveable in _validate_links.
fields.label: Closest Fabric Master

fields.description: How many catalogue rows folded into this recommendation. The recommender de-duplicates by scoring identity — 24,838 rows collapse to ~1,400 distinct specifications — so one row here can stand for several. The board selects the fold, not a variant.
fields.label: Variant Count

fields.description: JSON array of the distinct fabric codes behind the fold, capped by the recommender. Display only.
fields.label: Variant Codes

fields.description: Whether this fabric's batch has a photographed swatch. Lets the board show a no-image tile without a lookup per row, and is what decides whether image URLs are rebuilt on read at all.
fields.label: Has Image

fields.description: Legacy column from the get_matching_fabrics flow, still written and still read as the fallback for rows that predate `has_image`. New rows rebuild their URLs from `batch` instead.
fields.label: Image URL

fields.description: Legacy 0-100 score from get_matching_fabrics. The recommender's equivalents are match_score and fit_score.
fields.label: Relevancy Score

fields.description: The raw recommendation object verbatim, minus the rebuildable image_url/thumbnail. Nothing the recommender returns is lost, and a new field there needs no migration here.
fields.label: Raw Recommendation
